ETEL.note: H1-26: revenue +17%, net profit +47%, tariff increases approved, 5G rollout. Caution: profit swings with FX; price is above the analyst targets found.

SWDY.note: H1-26: revenue +32%, ~$6.5bn project backlog. Caution: net profit grew only 14% and margin is narrowing; price is above the analyst targets found.

TMGH.note: 2Q-26: net profit +21% to EGP 4.5bn, revenue +14%; H1 net +23%, strong contracted sales. Caution: property demand is sensitive to rates, inflation and cash collection.

EGAL.note: FY25/26: net profit +52% to EGP 15.5bn, revenue +23%. Caution: cyclical, depends on aluminium prices and energy costs.

MFPC.note: H1-26: net profit +70% to EGP 9.9bn, revenue +52%, ~80% exports, stable gas supply. Caution: gas supply and urea price swings.

ABUK.note: H1-26: net profit EGP 10.0bn on EGP 23.5bn revenue, plants at full capacity, capacity upgrade done. Caution: depends on gas supply and urea prices.

ORAS.note: H1-26: revenue +52%, net profit +90%, backlog $10.9bn (+14%), new awards +42%, data-center work. Caution: Q2 operating cash outflow; thin construction margins.

ALCN.note: H1-26: net profit +18% to EGP 3.8bn but revenue only +3%; AD Ports tender offer is a possible catalyst. Caution: profit growth is not coming from revenue growth.

EFIH.note: H1-26: net profit +64% to EGP 1.8bn on revenue +29% (EGP 4.2bn); FY25 net profit EGP 2.45bn (+34%). Caution: relies on government-linked payment business, and the price already reflects strong growth (roughly 28x trailing profit by my calculation).

ADIB.note: H1-26: net profit +21% to EGP 7.5bn, total income +25% to EGP 29.1bn; Q1 profit +20.5%. Caution: EPS fell to 4.98 from 7.43 (probably more shares after a capital increase, worth checking); bank earnings depend on rates and inflation.

FWRY.note: H1-26: revenue +39% to EGP 5.2bn, net profit +29% to EGP 1.6bn (31% margin), transaction value +52%, growth accelerated in Q2, neobanking and a medical platform planned for 2027. Caution: profit is growing slower than revenue; competition in payments.

ORHD.note: H1-26: net profit +4.5% to EGP 3.17bn (Q2 +26% to EGP 1.33bn), revenue +28.5% to EGP 14.8bn; excluding land sales profit +57.5%. Large deferred-revenue backlog. Caution: Q1 profit fell 16%, land-sale timing distorts quarters, and hospitality is exposed to regional tension.

EFID.note: H1-26: revenue +33% to EGP 12.3bn, net profit +63% to EGP 1.5bn, margin up to 12.2%, exports +52%. Caution: growth slowed in Q2 (profit +31% vs +102% in Q1); food input costs and FX.

PHDC.note: H1-26: revenue +25% to EGP 19.5bn and record EGP 284bn backlog, EGP 75bn of Ras El-Hekma sales in two weeks. Caution: net profit fell 7% to EGP 2.3bn and EBITDA margin dropped to 21% from 29%; Q1 drop was partly a one-off land sale last year.

JUFO.note: H1-26: sales +25% to EGP 17.7bn, net profit EGP 1.38bn vs 0.78bn (EPS 1.17 vs 0.66), Q1 profit more than doubled; recovering after a weak 2025 (profit -30%). Caution: margins swing with FX-linked raw-material costs and orange concentrate prices.

OCDI.note: H1-26: revenue +25% to EGP 6.0bn but net profit -36% to EGP 834m (Q1 -69%; Q2 looks stronger by my arithmetic). Large land bank, EGP 48bn 2025 sales and a $2.3bn MIDAR deal; majority-owned by Aldar/ADQ. Caution: profit is lumpy and below last year's.

GBCO.note: H1-26: revenue +35% to EGP 48bn but net profit -24.5% to EGP 1.26bn (2.6% margin); Q1 -30% and Q2 -21% on higher finance costs, provisions, FX losses and pressure in regional auto. New CBE securitization rules may raise GB Capital's funding costs. Strength: strong Egyptian car demand.

VLMRA.note: H1-26: revenue +13% to $392m, Q2 revenue +25%; reported profit -22% only because H1-25 had $44.8m one-offs (underlying +47%; top-5 subsidiaries +37%). Fertilizer revenue +31% on higher urea prices; UK Endolys project starts Q4-26. Caution: depends on urea prices and gas; holding company itself posted a standalone loss.

RAYA.note: H1-26: revenue +22% to EGP 33.8bn (Aman +38%, RCX +29%) but net profit -17% to EGP 739m on a thin margin; Q2 profit fell sharply (about -32% by my arithmetic). FY25 revenue +41%. Caution: profit is not following revenue; I did not find the cause.

EGCH.note: FY25/26 (to June): net profit +82% to EGP 1.79bn, revenue +31%. Caution: quarters are very uneven (9M profit was only EGP 531m, so Q4 alone was ~EGP 1.26bn, likely FX-driven), the FY26/27 budget targets lower profit (EGP 1.5bn), and EGP 6.8bn of debt is being restructured.

SCEM.note: H1-26: net profit +103% to EGP 1.56bn (EPS 5.99 vs 2.08), revenue +18% to EGP 4.7bn; majority-owned by Vicat. Caution: cement faces oversupply and fuel-cost pressure, and the very high Q1 net margin (~52%) suggests some non-operating gains.

CCAP.note: H1-26: back to profit (EGP 200m vs -EGP 1.3bn loss), Q2 profit EGP 2.0bn; revenue +52% to EGP 94.7bn, EBITDA +403%, interest costs -22%; raising its stake in the ERC refinery to 27% (closing Dec-26). Caution: the turnaround rests almost entirely on one refinery (ERC); refining margins are volatile, debt is large and the rest of the portfolio is flat (cement profit -61%).

AMOC.note: H1-26: net profit +114% to EGP 1.88bn (EPS 1.46 vs 0.68), sales +35% to EGP 26.2bn, operating cash flow turned positive; revised 2026 profit budget to EGP 2.1bn (double the original). Caution: refining margins are volatile and net margins are historically thin (2-5%), so the Q2 jump may not repeat.

ORWE.note: H1-26: net profit +83% to EGP 1.91bn on sales +10.6% to EGP 13.9bn; Q2 profit nearly doubled to EGP 1.1bn and net cash replaced net debt. Caution: part of the jump is one-offs (about EGP 300m capital gains; adjusted profit +64%) and faster export-subsidy collections; Egyptian household demand is weak.
